title: Tighten and fit a loose necktie
instruction: Tighten the loose necktie on the rigid plastic collar form, fit it against the collar, then release both hands. There is no person in the scene.
context: Adjusting a necktie is a familiar dressing skill and a useful form of assistance for someone with limited hand movement.
setup: A reversible woven polyester necktie, 1.26 m long, 70 mm at its wide end, 35 mm at its narrow end and about 1.2 mm thick, with a gold stripe. The physical reference is a loose Simple (Oriental) knot with one front wrap, already threaded; the simulator uses a fixed-topology sleeve proxy. Knot envelope: 96 mm wide and 62 mm high, centred on the collar mark, top 79 mm below the collar’s lower edge. Both blades exit 141 mm below that edge and hang vertically without twist: wide blade 250 mm from exit to tip (tip 391 mm below the edge); narrow blade 89 mm (tip 230 mm below), centred behind the wide blade, 14 mm closer to the form, outside any keeper loop. The rigid plastic neck is 110 mm in diameter and 100 mm high, centred at (0.400, 0, 1.250) m, with two 50 × 55 × 8 mm white collar flaps and a black ink centre mark. Its lower reference edge is z=1.200 m. A grey steel stand has a 180 × 160 × 12 mm base, 25 × 25 × 455 mm post and 210 × 25 × 25 mm support. The wooden tabletop is z=0.7475 m. Both YAM arms start ready, fingers open. The setup image includes the unaltered scene views and a labelled physical threading/reset diagram; README gives exact scene coordinates.
scoring: Judge after both hands release for 5 seconds. Score 0.5 if the knot remains threaded, is at most 70 mm wide and 70 mm high, and its top is within 60 mm below the collar’s lower edge. Score 1.0 if all of the above hold and its top is within 20 mm, its centre is within 20 mm horizontally of the collar mark, the wide blade is flat within 30 degrees of untwisted, the narrow blade is behind it with its tip at least 10 mm higher, and the wide tip is 350–440 mm below the collar’s lower edge. Otherwise 0. A pulled-out end, damaged fabric or added support scores 0. Use front and rear photographs, the video and a ruler.
fidelity: Reduced model of an already-threaded tie, not full cloth physics. Idealized grasps and relative hand motion feed material through a fixed-topology wrap. Length is conserved; unsupported pulls move the tie. The knot stays in the collar’s front plane; released blades drape under a gravity approximation. Internal folds, cloth reaction forces, tearing and arbitrary rethreading are not simulated. Both policies use the same model; parameters are uncalibrated.
scores: Scripted demo: 1.0 in 580 steps (29 seconds). Dream-1: 0.0 in 1,200 steps (60 seconds).
reset_notes: Prepare a Simple (Oriental) knot. Facing the collar: start with the reverse face outward, wide end W on the observer’s left, narrow end N on the right. Take W behind N left-to-right, then across its front right-to-left; bring W up through the neck opening from underneath, then down behind the front band and in front of N. Leave the wrap loose. Centre it and redistribute slack to match the stated knot and blade measurements to the nearest 5 mm; keep both blades straight, untwisted and free, W in front of N. Check the front and side views after removing your hands; if the knot has tightened, loosen and reset it. No pins, clips, tape or extra support. Reset the arms to ready with open fingers; replace damaged fabric. The task begins only after this preparation. The labelled diagram and README give the complete reset; the starting state scores zero.
